 4  L.A.C. No. 103/1995  JUDGMENT This reference made by the respondent No.1/BDA under Sections 30 and 31(2) of L.A. Act, 1894 (L.A. Act, 1894 for short), to determine the title and apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. Before proceeding further in the case, it is relevant to note that this court vide judgment dated 09- 06-2000 decided the claim of claimant No.1 to 8 and awarded  share together to claimant No.1 to 7 and  share to claimant No.8 in the acquired property and deposited compensation amount.
Therefore this case has been now tried in respect of remaining  share in the acquired property and deposited compensation amount.

.3. As per the records, the land involved in this case is the property bearing Sy. No.85/5 measuring 4 guntas of land, situated at Alahalli village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka vide Gazette notification bearing No.HUD 553-MNX 90 dated L.A.C. No. 103/1995 27.07.1991 for the purpose of formation of layout in J.P. Nagar 9th Phase has been acquired by the B.D.A. .4.

Initially this reference is made in the names Hanumantha and Narayana as claimants and this Court vide vide judgment dated 09.06.2000 passed the award holding that LRs of Hanumantha S/o Thoti Muniya,
who are claimants 1 to 7 are entitled for 1/4th share in the compensation.
Similarly one Narayana who is claimant No.8 is entitled for 1/4th share in the compensation amount and remaining amount has been kept in Fixed Deposits.

Subsequently claimants 9 to 12 impleaded in the case and they have filed claim statement claiming the right over the property and also claiming that the property originally belongs to one Thoti Hanumantha and the said Thoti Hanumantha had 4 sons namely (1)
Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa; (2) Doddaiah; (3) Muni Doddaiah and (4) Muniswamappa.
Further it is claimed that claimants 1 L.A.C. No. 103/1995 to 7 are surviving LRs of Muniswamappa have received  share in the compensation and claimant No.8 who is son of late.
Doddaiah has received  th share in the compensation deposited in the Court.

Now the claim statement filed by surviving LRs of Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa claiming that they are entitled for 1/4th Thoti Muniya Alias Hanumantha vs Spl.Lao Bda on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110849818/
3 share each in the compensation as they are successors of Thoti Hanumantha through his remaining 2 sons namely Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa and Muni Doddaiah.
.5.

sentences.text: After receipt of the reference, this court issued notice to both parties.
In pursuance of notice, the claimants had entered appearance and filed claim statement.
.6. The respondents have not filed objections to the above case.
.7. In order to prove their case, the claimant No.11(b) P. Saroja has been examined as PW.2 and no L.A.C. No. 103/1995 documents are marked.
But the claimants relied on the documents got marked by PW.1 in support of their claim.

.8. On the basis of the above, the points for consideration is that:
"Whether the claimants 9 to 12 prove that they are the absolute owners of the acquired property and entitled for the remaining  share in the compensation amount deposited to the Court?"
.9.

Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis, my finding on the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
REASONS .10.
Point:
As stated above, this reference is made to the Court under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act to determine the title of the claimants along with apportionment of the compensation.
As stated earlier, this Court entertained claim of claimants 1 to 8 vide L.A.C. No. 103/1995 judgment dated 09.06.2000.
As per the earlier judgment dated 09.06.2000, the claimants 1 to 7 are entitled for th share in the compensation amount and claimant No.8 is entitled for th share in the compensation amount.
Hence, no order has been passed by this Court in respect of remaining  share in the compensation amount.

.11. Subsequent to the passing of judgment dated 09.06.2000, the claimants 9 to 12 have been impleaded in this case claiming that they have  right over the acquired property and they are entitled for remaining  of compensation amount deposited to the court in this case.

Accordingly this now tried to decide claim of claimant No. 9 to 12 in respect of the remaining  share after the earlier judgment dated 09-06-2000.
.12.

As observed in the earlier judgment as well as admitted facts in this case is that the acquired property originally belongs to one Thoti Hanumantha L.A.C. No. 103/1995 and the said Thoti Hanumantha had 4 sons namely (1) Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa; (2) Doddaiah; (3)
Muni Doddaiah; and (4) Muniswamappa.

My learned predecessor in office while passing the judgment in this case dated 09.06.2000 specifically observed that the acquired property belongs to the sons of Thoti Hanumantha and the said Thoti Hanumantha had 4 sons and accordingly, four sons of Thoti Hanumantha are entitled for equal th share in the acquired property.

sentences.text: My learned predecessor in office in the judgment dated 09.06.2000 awarded the compensation to the surviving LRs of Muniswamappa who is younger son of Thoti Hanumantha as well as claimant No.8 who is son of late. Doddaiah and the said Doddaiah is the second son of Thoti Hanumantha.
As such, the Court already awarded compensation of th share each to two branches of LRs of Thoti Hanumantha.
Hence, two L.A.C. No. 103/1995 shares of remaining 2 sons of Thoti Hanumantappa to be decided in this case.
.14. In this case, till this date, nobody objected that Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa is not the son of Thoti Hanumantha.
As per claim of claimants 9 to 11, they are the surviving LRs of Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa and they have also filed the family tree.
As per the said document, this Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa had a wife by name Papamma and children by names (1) Doddannaia and (2) Munimalli.
The said Doddannaiah had a wife by name Muniyamma and daughter by name Jayalakshmi.
The said Munimalli W/o Pillappa had 2 children namely (1) P. Balaraj and (2) P. Saroja.

The said Muniyamma, Jayalakshmi, Munimalli, P. Balaraj and P. Saroja are claimants 9 to 11 being surviving members of branch of Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa, are entitled for 1/4th share in the compensation amount.

It is the case of the claimant No. 12(a) and 12(b) that Muni Doddaiah had no male issues, hence, Muni Doddaiah and his wife Dodda Muniyamma had a fostered son by name Pillappa and she has bequeathed her th share in the joint family properties in favour of Pillappa,
as such, these claimants 12(a) and (b) being children of fostered son Pillappa are entitled for the share of Muni Doddaiah who is 3 rd son of propositus Thoti Hanumantha.

Of course, the Will is not marked by the parties during the evidence of PW.2 but produced before the Court and certified copy of the Will produced before the Court discloses that the said Will already marked in the judicial proceedings before the competent Court.

As such, certainly the said Will can be accepted and it can be accepted that claimant No.12(a) and (b) are also entitled for th share along with share in the branch of Muniyappa @ Yettigalappa @ Hotteppa.
It is relevant to note that the claimant No.11 (a), 11 (b) and claimant12 (a), 12 (b) are one and same.
Claimant No. 12 (a), 12 (b) are impleded in the case as they are children of Munidoddaiah's foster son Pillappa.
It is not in dispute that the Pillappa is not the foster son of Munidoddaiah, hence it is to be accepted that Pillappa is the foster son of Munidoddaiah and his wife.
Therefore claimant No.12 (a), 12 (b) being the children of foster son Pillappa are entitled for the compensation to awarded to the branch of Munidoddaiah.

.17. In the evidence affidavit of PW.2 it is stated that claimant No. 11(a) and (b) are entitled for 1/8th share as claimant No. 11(a) and (b) being claimant No. 12(a) and (b) in this case also entitled for  th share in the compensation amount.
Hence, the claimant No. 12(a) and (b) are entitled for  th share in the compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.

In the result following:
L.A.C. No. 103/1995 ORDER The reference made under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in respect of claimant No.9 to 12 is hereby allowed.
